intro: AI didn't appear overnight — it took decades of research, failures, and breakthroughs to reach ChatGPT. This episode walks you through the full timeline from Alan Turing to Agentic AI. Use this summary to understand how each era of AI built on the last one.

sections.heading: What is Artificial Intelligence?
sections.definition: AI is the science of making machines perform tasks that normally need human intelligence — like recommending movies, driving cars, writing poems, or generating images. It's not magic; it's algorithms and data working together.
points: Machines doing human-like tasks = Artificial Intelligence
Examples: spam detection, face unlock, chatbots, image generation
AI won't replace your learning — you still need to understand and build
Modern AI is often called synthetic intelligence — machines going beyond simple rules

sections.heading: Early history (1950s–1980s)
sections.definition: It all started with Alan Turing asking 'Can a machine think?' in 1950. John McCarthy coined 'Artificial Intelligence' in 1956. Early AI relied on hand-written rules — hundreds of if-else conditions.
points: Turing Test: judge chats with human and machine — if judge can't tell, machine passes
1956: McCarthy names the field; researchers believe all intelligence can be simulated
Rule-based AI (Expert Systems): if email has 'FREE lottery' → mark as spam
Deep Blue (1997) beat chess champion Kasparov — but it used permutations, not true AI
AI Winter (1987–1993): funding dried up, hype faded, progress slowed

sections.heading: Machine Learning era
sections.definition: Rule-based systems failed because you can't write every possible condition. Machine Learning let computers learn patterns from data instead — show 10 lakh dog and cat images, and the machine learns to tell them apart.
points: Humans provide training data; machine finds patterns on its own
Works for classification: given an image, predict dog or cat
Still limited — couldn't handle every edge case or complex task
Needed human observation to prepare good training data

sections.heading: Deep Learning & Computer Vision
sections.definition: Inspired by human brain neurons, deep learning uses layered neural networks to learn complex patterns. GPU revolution and internet data made training on millions of images possible.
points: Neural networks mimic brain connections — layers of neurons processing data
2012 AlexNet on ImageNet (14M+ images) — breakthrough in image recognition
Enabled: face unlock, self-driving cars, X-ray analysis, product search in apps
Deep learning is a subset of ML focused on neural network-based learning

sections.heading: NLP & Transformers (2017)
sections.definition: Text seemed easy but was actually hard — same word, different meanings ('bank' of river vs 'Bank of India'). RNN and LSTM helped but struggled with long documents. Then came Transformers.
points: NLP challenges: ambiguous sentences like 'I saw a man with a telescope'
RNN/LSTM: processed text sequentially, limited context window
2017: Google paper 'Attention Is All You Need' — Transformers changed everything
Transformers understand context: 'it' in 'Lion did not cross because it cannot swim' → lion
All modern LLMs (GPT, Claude, Gemini) are built on Transformer architecture

sections.heading: LLMs, Gen AI & ChatGPT moment
sections.definition: LLMs are Transformers trained on massive internet data with huge compute power. Generative AI can create new content — text, images, videos — not just classify or recommend.
points: LLM needs: massive data + GPU/compute power (cost-intensive, few countries lead)
Gen AI generates new content — poems, code, images, videos
Nov 2022: ChatGPT launch — public could chat with AI for the first time
After ChatGPT: Gemini, Grok, DeepSeek, Claude — race continues
Modern AI: thinks, calls APIs, plans, writes code, searches web, works autonomously

sections.heading: Timeline recap
sections.definition: Keep these dates in mind — they show how fast AI evolved once Transformers arrived.
points: 1950 – Alan Turing | 1956 – John McCarthy names AI
50s–80s – Rule-Based AI | 1997 – Deep Blue beats Kasparov
90s – Machine Learning | 2000s – Deep Learning | 2012 – AlexNet
2016 – AlphaGo beats Lee Sedol | 2017 – Transformers
2022 – ChatGPT | 2025+ – Agentic AI era
